title: Horizontal positioning fixture hydraulic requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Open-circuit fixed-displacement hydraulic topology for the horizontal carriage. Tank feeds the pump suction; pump pressure branches directly to the main relief valve and the tandem-center 4/3 DCV. The relief valve and DCV tank port return directly to the tank. DCV work port A supplies the cap-side meter-in flow control, then the cap side of the dual pilot-operated check/load lock, then the cylinder cap chamber. DCV work port B supplies the rod-side meter-in flow control, then the rod side of the load lock, then the cylinder rod chamber. The one-way flow controls implement the selected non-compensated meter-in decisions in their controlled A-to-B directions; reverse free flow is internal to the selected one-way flow-control class. Cross-pilot release behavior is internal to the selected dual pilot-operated check valve because the catalog class exposes no separate pilot ports.

connections.notes: Pump pressure branch to main relief valve inlet.
Main relief discharge returns directly to reservoir.
Pump pressure branch to DCV pressure inlet.
DCV tank port returns directly to reservoir.
Cap-side commanded supply enters the cap meter-in flow control in its controlled A-to-B direction.
Cap-side metered outlet feeds the valve-side cap path of the dual pilot-operated check.
Cap-side load-lock actuator port connects directly to the cylinder cap chamber.
Rod-side commanded supply enters the rod meter-in flow control in its controlled A-to-B direction.
Rod-side metered outlet feeds the valve-side rod path of the dual pilot-operated check.
Rod-side load-lock actuator port connects directly to the cylinder rod chamber.

motion_control_decisions.justification: Horizontal resistive advance load; meter-in supply control is acceptable because the load is not gravity-aided or overrunning, and load-independent speed was not specified.
Static holding is required at any point after stopping or command release; a static load-locking strategy is required, not dynamic counterbalance control for this horizontal resistive load.
Horizontal resistive return load; meter-in supply control is acceptable because the load is not gravity-aided or overrunning, and load-independent speed was not specified.

component_states.reason: Catalog state routes P-A and B-T for cylinder extension.
Normal non-overpressure operating state during commanded advance; relief opens only if pressure reaches its setting.

phase_configurations.notes: Cap-side supply follows DCV.A -> CapMeterInFlowControl.A -> CapMeterInFlowControl.B -> LoadLock.A1 -> LoadLock.A2 -> Cylinder.Cap. Rod-side exhaust uses the selected components' internal reverse/pilot-released behavior back through the rod branch to DCV.B and DCV.T.

component_states.reason: Catalog tandem-center neutral unloads P-T while A and B are blocked.
Normal non-overpressure hold state; relief opens only if pressure reaches its setting.

phase_configurations.notes: On command release the DCV spring-centers to neutral. LoadLock blocks reverse outflow from both actuator chambers unless opposite work-line pressure is present.

component_states.reason: Catalog state routes P-B and A-T for cylinder retraction.
Normal non-overpressure operating state during commanded return; relief opens only if pressure reaches its setting.

phase_configurations.notes: Rod-side supply follows DCV.B -> RodMeterInFlowControl.A -> RodMeterInFlowControl.B -> LoadLock.B1 -> LoadLock.B2 -> Cylinder.Rod. Cap-side exhaust uses the selected components' internal reverse/pilot-released behavior back through the cap branch to DCV.A and DCV.T.

design_decisions.decision: Selected a 4/3 DCV rather than 4/2 because advance, return, and safe neutral hold modes are required.
design_decisions.rationale: The carriage requires extend, retract, and neutral operating modes; a spring-centered 4/3 DCV provides all three hydraulic states for a double-acting cylinder.

design_decisions.decision: Selected tandem-center DCV with fixed-displacement pump to unload pump flow to tank in neutral while work ports are blocked; pilot check valve provides leakage-resistant holding rather than relying on the DCV spool.
design_decisions.rationale: Spring-centered neutral stops commanded actuator flow, but DCV spool leakage is not treated as positive load holding; the load lock supplies the holding function while the tandem center unloads pump flow.

design_decisions.decision: Selected one-way non-compensated flow controls because the typed motion decisions require non-compensated meter-in control and no load-independent speed was specified.
design_decisions.rationale: For a resistive horizontal load, inlet metering is acceptable; one control on the cap branch sets advance speed and one on the rod branch sets return speed, while internal reverse checks allow opposite-side exhaust.

design_decisions.decision: Selected a dual pilot-operated check valve at the actuator because the hold decision requires pilot_check load locking for both cylinder chambers.
design_decisions.rationale: A double pilot-operated check/load-lock arrangement at the cylinder ports blocks outflow from both chambers in neutral and releases during commanded motion by opposite work-line pressure.

design_decisions.decision: Retained a main relief valve to limit system pressure no higher than the 100 bar project maximum; actual setting is deferred to sizing/implementation.
design_decisions.rationale: The pump pressure branch must have an overpressure path to tank, especially with a fixed-displacement supply and blocked or restricted downstream paths.

design_decisions.decision: No separate hydraulic pilot-line connections were added for LoadLock.
design_decisions.rationale: The selected generic dual pilot-operated check exposes only A1, A2, B1, and B2 ports; cross-pilot release is represented as conditional internal behavior requiring pressure at the opposite valve-side work port.

assumptions: Cylinder bore, rod diameter, pump displacement/flow, relief setting margin, and flow-control settings are sizing/implementation tasks, not topology selections.
The dual pilot-operated check valve's cross-pilot behavior is internal to the selected generic class because no separate pilot ports are listed in the catalog metadata.
Electrical command wiring, solenoid interlocks, pump drive hardware, filters, gauges, coolers, hoses, and manifolds are outside this topology build and are not instantiated.
open_issues: Cylinder bore, rod size, stroke, pump flow, relief setting margin, and flow-control settings are deferred to sizing and implementation.

Hydraulic catalog does not represent electrical command logic; implementation must ensure advance and return solenoid commands cannot be active simultaneously and must spring-center on command release.
Filters, screens, gauges, and other accessories are outside the topology component boundary and are not selected here.

research_coverage.summary: The evidence is strong for the open-circuit power/relief/return path, the double-acting-cylinder plus 4/3 directional-valve directional-control pattern, meter-in speed control for extend/retract, and leak-resistant static holding using double pilot-operated check/lock valves. However, one critical motion-profile requirement remains incomplete: the findings do not yet support an automatic phase-transition/control-sequence pattern for advancing, holding at position, and returning the carriage. Load holding is mostly supported for static neutral holding, but the findings themselves leave a safety-critical boundary condition weak: when pilot-operated checks are sufficient versus when counterbalance/over-center valves are required for controlled motion under overrunning or gravity-assisted loads.

items.rationale: T1 provides cited guidance for a complete open-circuit power and return topology: reservoir to pump inlet with inlet screen, pump outlet/pressure line to working circuit, relief valve from pressure side to tank/reservoir for overpressure protection, return-line filtration before tank, and submerged return to reduce foaming. It also covers the consequence of blocked flow/deadheading and the need for a relief/unloading path. The 100 bar limit is project-specific rather than externally cited, but the relief-valve set-pressure function is supported.

T2 gives cited component and connection guidance for a double-acting cylinder controlled by a 4-way/3-position spring-centered directional valve, including P/T/work-port connections, extension routing to cap end, retraction routing to rod end, and neutral behavior. It also distinguishes closed-center and tandem-center neutral implications and warns that the DCV spool alone is not adequate for load holding. T4 further supports compatibility of a 4-way DCV with pilot-operated lock valves.

T3 covers the requested meter-in placement for advance and return: cap-end meter-in during extension, rod-end meter-in during retraction, separate one-way flow controls for different speeds, and free reverse flow through bypass checks. However, the need also asks for an automatic phase-transition pattern. The accumulated findings do not provide cited guidance for how the circuit detects end-of-advance/hold completion/return command or automatically transitions among advance, hold, and return phases using limit valves, sequence valves, pressure switches, timers/PLC with solenoid DCV, detented/piloted valves, or equivalent controls.

T4 supports leak-resistant static holding with double pilot-operated check/lock valves at both cylinder work ports and explains pilot release during commanded motion. T2 supports why spool-center blocking alone is unsafe due to leakage/creep. This is enough for neutral/static holding in many resistive-load cases. The weak point is controlled-motion safety under an overrunning or gravity-assisted load: the findings explicitly state that the counterbalance-valve distinction is weak and should be researched before making a firm rule. Because the need is safety-critical and says uncontrolled motion must be prevented at the actuator, this boundary condition remains incomplete.

T2 and T4 together support the required leak-resistant neutral holding behavior: spring-centering returns the DCV to neutral on command release; the DCV spool must not be relied on as the holding element; double pilot-operated check/lock valves block flow from both cylinder ends in neutral; and commanded pressure from a 4-way valve pilots the opposite check open during motion. This covers stop-at-any-point static holding and safe neutralization, subject to the remaining nonresolved controlled-motion/overrunning-load boundary captured under the actuator holding need.

missing_or_weak_information: Missing critical claim for function_position_carriage_motion_profile: a cited automatic phase-transition/control-sequence pattern that connects the advance, hold-at-position, and return phases, including the component class used to sense/trigger phase changes and how it actuates or pilots the directional-control valve.

Missing critical safety boundary for function_position_carriage_holding: cited guidance distinguishing when double pilot-operated check valves are adequate for static carriage holding versus when counterbalance/over-center valves are required to prevent uncontrolled or overrunning actuator motion during release/movement.

design_review.summary: The proposed topology functionally satisfies the brief: it provides a complete open-circuit suction, pressure, relief, return, and work-port circuit; spring-centered 4/3 directional control for advance, return, and neutral; meter-in non-compensated speed control on the correct supply chamber for both extend and retract; and a dual pilot-operated check/load-lock at the cylinder ports for leakage-resistant holding at any point after command release. No blocking topology issues were found.

validation.summary: Deterministic validation: valid. Engineering review: valid. No blocking topology issues were found.
